label: EdgeRouter 6 PoE
description: EdgeRouter 6 PoE (ER-6P) - 5x 1G RJ45 + 1x 1G SFP. 16 W max.

poe.note: Ubiquiti prints no total PoE budget on either surface. The tech-spec page states the PoE interface ((5) 24V Passive PoE ports (2-pair and 4-pair)), the included 60 W (24 V, 2.5 A) AC/DC adapter, "Max. power consumption 16 W (excluding PoE output)" and "Max. PoE wattage per port: 24 W (24 V, 1 A, 4-pair); 12 W (24 V, 0.5 A, 2-pair)". The 44 W recorded here is the arithmetic of that stated configuration - 60 W adapter minus 16 W of device draw leaves 44 W for the passive ports - and is an envelope derived from two printed figures, not a budget Ubiquiti prints. A lab that fits a larger 16-30 V DC supply can declare its own.

notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti's own tech-spec page (read 2026-11-19, HTTP 200, 582,715 B): Networking interface **(5) GbE RJ45 ports, (1) 1G SFP port**; PoE interface **(5) 24V Passive PoE ports (2-pair and 4-pair)**; Power method **AC/DC power adapter, 24V, 2.5A (Included)**; Power supply **AC/DC adapter, external, 60W**; Supported voltage range **16-30V DC**; Max. power consumption **16W (Excluding PoE output)**; Max. PoE wattage per port **24W (24V, 1A, 4-pair) / 12W (24V, 0.5A, 2-pair)**. store.ui.com/us/en/products/er-6p (200, 332,139 B) prints the same table. No datasheet: dl.ui.com/ds/er-6p_ds.pdf answers 302 to the techspecs root (609,911 B) and dl.ui.com/qig/er-6p/ 200s an iframe shell, so both figures above are tech-spec-only. The five copper ports are 24 V passive, not 802.3af - the port class says so, and no 48 V standard is claimed.
